findings.detail: The first candidate omitted content from the write_file provider schema required list while the host still required it; a red regression test and 047de49 restored path+content.
Removing the duplicated provider schemas left hashlib unused and would fail the CI E9/F gate; 047de49 removed it and ruff passed.
Unknown property names were copied unbounded into the recoverable error envelope; a red test and f772f55 bounded the diagnostic to fixed-size ASCII.
An unpaired surrogate in an unknown property name could fail UTF-8 trace writing; f772f55 escapes names through ASCII backslashreplace and the regression test covers it.

why: PC-TCONTRACT-1 joins provider tool declarations, host argument validation, trace summaries and task-policy names behind one closed contract.
not_doing: No new tool, shell execution, command-template expansion, provider call, default enablement, release or publication action.
diff_walk: pocketchat/tool_contracts.py: declares the three closed tool schemas, bounded argument parsing, per-contract hashes and ASCII-bounded diagnostics.
pocketchat/provider.py: derives provider offers and trace summaries from the shared contracts and removes unused hashing.
pocketchat/session.py: validates model arguments before file or memory I/O and uses the validated values for execution.
pocketchat/task_policy.py: imports the task-policy tool names from the same contract.
tests and bilingual docs: cover default-off payloads, schema agreement, unknown/missing/oversized/malformed arguments, no I/O on refusal and compatibility wording.
static_checks: All three provider schemas and host validators derive from CONTRACTS.
Unknown or missing arguments are refused before permission or tool-start events.
Diagnostics are at most 160 ASCII characters and never include unbounded model property names.
Command templates remain closed argv records executed without a shell.
